A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with VLMIG renamed LaMI and many main results retained. Text, equations, figures, tables, and both versions' appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative outputs in Sections 5–6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional comparisons, ablations, and qualitative cases in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The frozen LLM and vision encoder, trainable visual projector, late-fusion attention, and CLIP-weighted combination of image-conditioned and text-only predictions remain. Renaming and added descriptions of batched generation do not establish an algorithm change; SDXL-turbo already appears in v1. v2's introductory entropy-weighting language is not accompanied by a different operational fusion rule.

E1.justification: The proposed model's training corpora and named benchmark suites remain. Qualitative coverage changes: v1 Figure 2's open-ended beach-description generation example disappears, while v2 Section 5 adds individual negation and legendary-knowledge cases. These are limited scenario changes, not new benchmark suites.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds fine-tuned BERT/GPT-2 controls and removes RoBERTa-based X-adapter, T5-based LIVE, and iNLG comparisons. v1's OPT-2.7B/BLIP-2 comparison block disappears; v2 Table 4 adds comparisons involving Vicuna, InstructBLIP, Llava-Next, and Qwen2-VL. A runtime-matched Best-of-N comparator is also added.

E3.justification: New protocols include Gemma-2B Best-of-N sampling calibrated to LaMI's runtime at k=6 and instruction-style top-1 evaluation for added instruction models. Fusion ablations now cross fusion location with single/multiple images on GPT-2 object tasks. The image-versus-embedding comparison expands from Color/PIQA/BoolQ to aggregate visual commonsense, reasoning, and reading-comprehension evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds joint fusion/multi-image ablations, a compute-budget control, aggregation-strategy comparisons, generation-versus-retrieval testing, and explicit success/failure cases. It removes v1's Gemma fine-tuning control, CLIP-versus-DINOv2, SDXL-turbo-versus-SD-turbo, and sentence-selection studies. The image-count curve remains, while the earlier early/prepend/late-fusion study is replaced by a different comparison.

E5.justification: v1 Section 3.2 explicitly states that images generated from the same sentence use unique seeds; v2 omits this disclosure. Neither version reports repeated-evaluation counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. This is a limited change in seed reporting, not demonstrated statistical reliability.

E6.justification: Many shared aggregate results remain identical, including Gemma-2B's 50.1/65.1/48.9 scores. New model, control, retrieval, and timing results appear, while v1's detailed Tables 9–12 disappear. Table 1 changes Vokenization Relative Size from 48.3 to 72.4 and Z-LaVI from 56.2 to 76.8; Z-LaVI Object Shape changes from 64.3 to 64.4. These reported changes do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 corrects Equation 1 from minimizing log likelihood to maximizing it, resolving the conflict with v1's stated negative-log-likelihood objective. It also uses projected visual embeddings uv instead of raw zv in attention keys/values, fixing a dimensional inconsistency. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains late fusion plus multiple generated images to improve visual commonsense while preserving textual reasoning. v2 additionally emphasizes efficient adaptation and modest inference overhead, and distinguishes outperforming visually augmented LMs from matching VLMs on visual tasks. These refine the comparative and efficiency claims without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains text-only fallback under negation and failures when high CLIP alignment favors factually incorrect legendary imagery. Its limitations discussion reframes latency as test-time scaling and explicitly acknowledges unevaluated recent reasoning models and training limited to 8B parameters. v1 chiefly discusses latency and an embedding alternative; interpretations supporting its removed encoder, generator, and prompt-selection studies also disappear.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A newly specifies CLIP-ViT-B/32, default k=6, training GPU-hours, and baseline data provenance. It omits v1's constant learning-rate schedule, GeLU and projector-width specification, and detailed sentence-selection procedure. The abstract replaces the direct code/model access pointer with a project-page pointer. These materially change reproducibility documentation without proving corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: The Multiple Generations Agreement discussion and its consistency/confidence-estimation references are removed. v2 adds work including MORE and Language Is Not All You Need, and positions visual augmentation within test-time scaling through Wei, Yao, and Snell, alongside a DeepSeek-R1 applicability boundary. X-adapter's citation-year update represents the same work and is not an additional contribution.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten and condensed. Experimental settings move largely into Appendix A. Separate qualitative analysis, conclusions, limitations, and ethical-considerations sections replace the earlier organization.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensively restructured comparison tables and new control/ablation displays. The architecture diagram is retained as Figure 2, and the image-count plot remains Figure 3. The ferret/beach illustration is replaced by a first-page penguin example, while detailed appendix tables are removed.

improvement.justification: The runtime-matched baseline and joint fusion/multi-image ablations strengthen evidence for the central design choices, while concrete failure cases clarify applicability. These provide a limited net improvement. The benefit is tempered by removal of per-task results and useful encoder/generator/prompt ablations, lost implementation details, and incomplete specification of the Best-of-N runtime control, including its selected N.
